newsitem.title: DENMARK: FOCUS-Record profit for Denmark's BG Bank.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Record profit for Denmark's BG Bank.

text.p: Denmark's third biggest bank, BG Bank, on Tuesday reported record first-half 1997 profits, boosted by solidly better core earnings, which it predicted would be higher for the full year than in 1996.
BG Bank's first-half result, the first to be announced by one of Denmark's big three banks, showed an almost 30 percent rise in pre-tax profits to 1.063 billion crowns from 821 million last year.
"We consider our pre-tax interim result to be satisfactory. Our expectations for core earnings for the full year exceed 1996," the bank said in a statement accompanying its results.
The bank's core earnings rose 31 percent compared with the same 1996 period, fuelled by substantial net interest and fees income and dramatically lower losses and bad debt provisions.
Operating profits for the six months were 989 million crowns against 754 million a year ago.
BG said net interest and fees earnings, some five percent up at 3.194 billion crowns, helped core earnings despite 3.6 percent higher costs.

A steep fall in losses and bad debt provisions for the period to 175 million crowns from 297 million crowns a year ago was also seen as a factor contributing to BG Bank's improved first-half result, which was above analysts' expectations.
Analysts had tipped an average 1.177 billion crown first-half 1997 result before tax and extraordinary items, whereas the bank posted a 1.250 billion interim profit.

BG had previously predicted 1997 earnings slightly lower than 1996's record 1.665 billion crowns but upgraded its forecast on publication of its 1997 first half figures, which showed core earnings of 968 million crowns.
The results had little effect on the bank's share price, which closed at 390 crowns, up one crown.
The statement said that the bank expected continued growth in deposits and borrowing but that narrowing spreads meant that net interest earnings would not grow.
After the cancellation last June of its alliance with mortgage lender Nykredit and insurer Topdanmark, BG said it would buy back its own shares held by Nykredit.
BG has begun to put those shares back on the market -- it says it has already sold about half -- and some analysts contacted by Reuters feared that continued sales might put BG stock under pressure.

According to a recent survey conducted by Reuters, Denmark's biggest banks are headed for record first-half results this month, boosted by continuing falls in losses and bad debt provisions and solid securities gains.
Denmark's two biggest banks, Den Danske Bank and Unidanmark, are due to unveil their first-half 1997 results on August 21. -- Copenhagen newsroom +45-33969652
